query: For reported HfNbTiVAl10 with a hierarchical heterostructure, what testable hypothesis could enable Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture-related behavior to be predicted more rapidly and accurately under tensile and fracture testing than with established simulations? State the hypothesized rationale, the measurable gains in predictive accuracy and efficiency, circumstances in which the hypothesis may fail, relevant supporting evidence, and a predeclared result from independent measurements that would decisively falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Integrating a machine learning surrogate model that explicitly incorporates hierarchical heterostructure descriptors—extracted via in situ microstructural characterization—will enable rapid and accurate predictions of Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior of HfNbTiVAl10 under tensile and fracture testing, outperforming established simulation methods.
generation.material_initial_state: HfNbTiVAl10 alloy prepared with an intrinsic hierarchical heterostructure featuring a mix of ordered and disordered phases, nanoprecipitates, and phase boundaries.
generation.intervention: Develop and deploy a machine learning model that is trained on microstructural features (e.g., precipitate size/distribution, dislocation structure, phase fraction, and grain boundary character) obtained from rapid characterization methods (such as electron microscopy and diffraction analysis) alongside mechanical testing data.
generation.conditions: Testing under controlled tensile loading at room temperature (and selected elevated temperatures) with a range of strain rates; the ML model predictions will be benchmarked against established finite-element and CALPHAD-based simulation results.
generation.structural_mediator: The hierarchical heterostructure acting as the mediator by governing load transfer, plastic deformation mechanisms, and crack propagation paths.
generation.mechanism: Microstructural features, captured through high-resolution characterization, provide quantitative inputs that correlate with mechanical performance. The ML model exploits these correlations to predict mechanical properties more efficiently by bypassing computationally expensive iterative simulations.
generation.predicted_outcome: The ML model will predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture-related behavior with an average error below 10%, achieving a computational speedup of at least 5× relative to traditional simulation methods.
generation.baseline: Standard finite-element and CALPHAD simulation approaches that typically yield prediction errors above 15% and require longer computation times.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis may fail if the hierarchical heterostructure of HfNbTiVAl10 evolves in an unexpected manner under extreme strain rates or temperatures, or if key microstructural descriptors are not reliably captured due to noise or resolution limits in experimental characterization.
generation.uncertainty: It remains uncertain whether all fracture mechanisms, particularly those involving sub-micron crack propagation or dynamic phase transformations, are adequately characterized by the chosen descriptors and thus fully captured by the ML model.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare HfNbTiVAl10 samples and perform detailed in situ microstructural characterization followed by tensile and fracture tests under a range of controlled conditions. Train the machine learning surrogate model using these microstructural descriptors and mechanical test results to predict the modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior. Compare the predictions with those from established simulation methods as well as independent experimental measurements.
measurements: Microstructural integrity before and after testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ML model predictions show an average error exceeding 15% compared to experimental outcomes or if the computational times are not significantly reduced relative to traditional simulation methods (i.e., speedup less than 5×), the hypothesis is decisively falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractThe aim of this work was to provide a guidance to the prediction and design of high-entropy alloys with good performance. New promising compositions of refractory high-entropy alloys with the desired phase composition and mechanical properties (yield strength) have been predicted using a combination of machine learning, phenomenological rules and CALPHAD modeling. The yield strength prediction in a wide range of temperatures (20–800 °C) was made using a surrogate model based on a support-vector machine algorithm. The yield strength at 20 °C and 600 °C was predicted quite precisely (the average prediction error was 11% and 13.5%, respectively) with a decrease in the precision to slightly higher than 20% at 800 °C. An Al13Cr12Nb20Ti20V35 alloy with an excellent combination of ductility and yield strength at 20 °C (16.6% and 1295 MPa, respectively) and at 800 °C (more 50% and 898 MPa, respectively) was produced based on the prediction.Keywords: high-entropy alloys, machine learning, prediction, strength, structure
